info_cards.fact: "The Kite" by Francisco Goya. An early tapestry-design painting by Goya showing young men flying a kite outdoors.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Two Tahitian Women
info_cards.fact: "Two Tahitian Women" by Paul Gauguin. A painting from Gauguin's time in Tahiti, known for its bold tropical colours.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
info_cards.fact: "Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?" by Paul Gauguin. A large, philosophical painting exploring the stages of human life.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Yellow Christ
info_cards.fact: "The Yellow Christ" by Paul Gauguin. A Post-Impressionist painting showing a crucifix scene in a Brittany landscape.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Bedroom
info_cards.fact: "The Bedroom" by Vincent van Gogh. Another version of Van Gogh's painting of his simple bedroom in Arles.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Irises
info_cards.fact: "Irises" by Vincent van Gogh. A vivid painting of purple irises growing in a garden.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Almond Blossoms
info_cards.fact: "Almond Blossoms" by Vincent van Gogh. A painting of blooming almond branches against a blue sky, made to celebrate a birth in his family.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: The Potato Eaters
info_cards.fact: "The Potato Eaters" by Vincent van Gogh. An early Van Gogh painting showing a poor farming family sharing a meal.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Sunflowers in a Vase
info_cards.fact: "Sunflowers in a Vase" by Vincent van Gogh. Another of Van Gogh's sunflower still-life paintings made in Arles.

info_cards.title: Famous Painting: Boulevard Montmartre
info_cards.fact: "Boulevard Montmartre" by Camille Pissarro. An Impressionist street scene of a busy Paris boulevard.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Abraham Lincoln: The Man (Standing Lincoln)
info_cards.fact: "Abraham Lincoln: The Man (Standing Lincoln)" by Augustus Saint-Gaudens. A bronze statue of President Lincoln standing in Chicago's Lincoln Park.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Puck Statue
info_cards.fact: "The Puck Statue" by Frederick William MacMonnies. A bronze statue of the mischievous character Puck atop a New York building.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Dreaming Girl
info_cards.fact: "The Dreaming Girl" by Edward Berge. A bronze fountain sculpture of a sleeping figure, in Baltimore's Wyman Park.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Storyteller
info_cards.fact: "The Storyteller" by Glenna Goodacre. A bronze public sculpture celebrating the tradition of oral storytelling.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Vietnam Women's Memorial
info_cards.fact: "Vietnam Women's Memorial" by Glenna Goodacre. A bronze sculpture in Washington, D.C., honouring women who served during the Vietnam War.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Ireland's Famine Memorial
info_cards.fact: "Ireland's Famine Memorial" by Rowan Gillespie. A group of bronze statues in Dublin honouring those who endured the Great Famine.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: The Matchstick Men
info_cards.fact: "The Matchstick Men" by Sean Hanley (after L. S. Lowry). Public sculptures inspired by a beloved English painter's depiction of working-class life.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Bronze Lions of Trafalgar Square
info_cards.fact: "Bronze Lions of Trafalgar Square" by Edwin Landseer. Four large bronze lion statues guarding the base of Nelson's Column in London.

info_cards.title: Famous Sculpture: Eros Statue (Piccadilly Circus)

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Marcus Aurelius
info_cards.fact: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realize this, and you will find strength." — Roman emperor and Stoic philosopher whose personal writings, Meditations, remain widely read today.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Lao Tzu
info_cards.fact: "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step." — Ancient Chinese philosopher traditionally credited as the founder of Taoism and author of the Tao Te Ching.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Ibn Khaldun
info_cards.fact: "History is a science... it has a great utility, an honorable purpose, since it makes us acquainted with the conditions of past nations." — Arab historian and scholar often regarded as a founder of sociology and historiography.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Maimonides
info_cards.fact: "Teach thy tongue to say 'I do not know,' and thou shalt progress." — Medieval Jewish philosopher and physician whose writings shaped Jewish law and philosophy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Thomas Aquinas
info_cards.fact: "To one who has faith, no explanation is necessary. To one without faith, no explanation is possible." — Italian Dominican friar and philosopher whose writings blended Christian theology with Aristotelian philosophy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Voltaire
info_cards.fact: "Common sense is not so common." — French Enlightenment writer and philosopher known for his advocacy of free speech and religious tolerance.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: John Locke
info_cards.fact: "The discipline of desire is the background of character." — English philosopher whose ideas about natural rights influenced modern democracy and the U.S. Constitution.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Mary Wollstonecraft
info_cards.fact: "I do not wish women to have power over men, but over themselves." — English writer and philosopher often considered a founder of feminist philosophy for her book A Vindication of the Rights of Woman.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Immanuel Kant
info_cards.fact: "Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law." — German philosopher whose work on ethics and reason deeply influenced modern philosophy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Friedrich Nietzsche
info_cards.fact: "He who has a why to live for can bear almost any how." — German philosopher known for his ideas on morality, culture, and the concept of the 'will to power.'

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Soren Kierkegaard
info_cards.fact: "Life is not a problem to be solved, but a reality to be experienced." — Danish philosopher often considered the first existentialist philosopher.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Simone de Beauvoir
info_cards.fact: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." — French philosopher and writer whose book The Second Sex became a foundational text of feminist theory.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Bertrand Russell
info_cards.fact: "The whole problem with the world is that fools and fanatics are always so certain of themselves." — British philosopher and mathematician who won the Nobel Prize in Literature for his wide-ranging humanist writing.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Hannah Arendt
info_cards.fact: "The sad truth is that most evil is done by people who never make up their minds to be either good or evil." — German-American political theorist known for her writings on totalitarianism and political power.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Rumi
info_cards.fact: "Let yourself be silently drawn by the strange pull of what you really love." — 13th-century Persian poet and Sufi mystic whose poetry remains widely read and translated today.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Al-Farabi
info_cards.fact: "The First Cause is the cause of the existence of every other existent." — Medieval philosopher known as 'the Second Teacher' (after Aristotle) for his influence on Islamic philosophy.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Averroes (Ibn Rushd)
info_cards.fact: "Ignorance leads to fear, fear leads to hatred, and hatred leads to violence." — Andalusian philosopher and judge whose commentaries on Aristotle influenced both Islamic and European thought.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Zhuangzi
info_cards.fact: "Flow with whatever may happen, and let your mind be free." — Ancient Chinese philosopher whose writings, alongside Lao Tzu's, form a foundation of Taoist thought.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Mencius
info_cards.fact: "The great man is he who does not lose his child's heart." — Chinese philosopher and follower of Confucius whose writings shaped Confucian thought on human nature.

info_cards.title: Notable Person: Seneca
info_cards.fact: "Luck is what happens when preparation meets opportunity." — Roman Stoic philosopher and statesman whose letters and essays remain widely studied today.
